reasoning: Both attempts draw ghosts on each client, draw the player's own ghost locally every frame, and pass all checks. A meets the network and security criteria much better: it uses an UnreliableRemoteEvent with sequence ordering, rate-limits each player with a token bucket on the server, and never echoes updates back to the builder. B keeps ghost traffic on reliable remotes, has no server-side rate limit, and uses FireAllClients, which echoes each builder's updates back. B's batching and zero idle traffic are nice, but they don't make up for those gaps.

criteria.note: updateLocalGhost sends on change, at most SEND_RATE=20/s and independent of FPS, but also resends every RESEND_INTERVAL=1s, so an idle player sends 1/s.
The server keeps no parts and FireClient-relays the packet. Clients create parts with createGhostPart and smooth them.
localGhost.CFrame is set from getCursorCell each RenderStepped, with no round trip.
